title: Mouse without borders says keys dont match, when it does
author: Jebarson
summary: Mouse Without Borders rejects pairing between 0.100.x and 0.101.x peers as InvalidKey; a corroborating reporter confirmed that updating the older peer restores connectivity.

status.label: Known version-mismatch behavior
status.detail: Version mismatch reporting is already tracked by Issue 29794; no separate code fix belongs in this report.

next_action.label: Post matching-version guidance
next_action.reason: Document the confirmed recovery and consolidate the error-message gap with its existing tracker.

judgment.rationale: Both reports use 0.100.x paired with 0.101.2362.0, and the corroborating reporter confirmed that updating the older peer restores operation. Clearer version-mismatch reporting is already tracked by Issue 29794.
evidence: The original report pairs PowerToys 0.101.2362.0 with 0.100.0.0 and records InvalidKey.
The sole comment reproduces the problem between 0.100.2 and 0.101.2362.0 and confirms updating resolves it.
PRs 48742 and 49600 changed encrypted-stream framing and key derivation and require all peers to use the same version.
Issue 29794 tracks explicit version-mismatch detection, and Issue 41916 was closed as its duplicate.
judgment.recommended_action: Advise updating every peer to the same current version, without regenerating the existing key, and consolidate the reporting improvement under Issue 29794.

fix_assessment.rationale: A separate PowerToys code fix for this report would duplicate Issue 29794's version-mismatch reporting work. Mixed-version compatibility is not the appropriate fix for intentional protocol and derivation changes.

issue_context.summary: The reported InvalidKey result follows intentional cross-version protocol changes, not evidence that the displayed key text differs.
known_information: The visible key was copied between the peers.
Both reported reproductions used different PowerToys versions.
Updating the older peer restored operation for the corroborating reporter.
The 0.101 release introduced deliberate encrypted-stream framing and PBKDF2 changes.
inferences: InvalidKey is a generic handshake-failure classification and does not prove that the entered key text differs.
Either versioned cryptographic change can prevent a 0.100 peer from decoding the newer stream.
issue_context.analysis: The precise cross-version recovery and existing owner make diagnostic collection and an independent design unnecessary. The action corrects the guidance to avoid unnecessary re-pairing.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue and comment.
Compared the 0.100 and 0.101 encryption paths and release history.
Reviewed Encryption.cs, SocketStuff.cs, DATA.cs, related Issues 29794 and 41916, and PRs 48742 and 49600.

actions.label: Post matching-version Mouse Without Borders guidance

comment.body: Thanks for the peer and status details. The additional report confirms that Mouse Without Borders can reject pairing when the machines use PowerToys 0.100.x and 0.101.x, and that updating the older installation restores the connection. Please update every peer to the same current PowerToys version and try again; the existing key should continue to work, so generating a new key is not necessary. The clearer version-mismatch reporting needed here is tracked in #29794.
